chains.title: GATA3 binds the alt allele more strongly at a TOX3 distal enhancer and increases breast cancer risk

links.claim: GATA3 is the best-supported GATA factor here: it is highly expressed and occupied over the variant in MCF7, and both the GATA3 own-model QBiC-SELEX result and the stronger GATA2-mapped GATA model detect an alt-increasing binding change with a strong alt site; ChIP occupancy itself is not allele-specific.

The variant lies in the ENSR16_9QTBS enhancer and in the EH38E3180851 distal enhancer-like cCRE with DNase and H3K27ac marks, supporting an active regulatory element, although these marks are maxima over biosamples and not allele-specific.

TOX3 is the nearest protein-coding gene at 17.5 kb and is the Open Targets L2G target for breast-cancer credible sets at this variant, but this variant has no significant GTEx v8 eQTL in breast or other tissues, so the enhancer-to-TOX3 link remains genetic/computational rather than expression-QTL-proven.
MCF7 is relevant because GATA3 is expressed at very high levels there and MCF-7 GATA3 ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant.

The T allele is the strongest reported breast-cancer effect allele and the credible set maps to TOX3, so alt-enhanced GATA3 binding could raise TOX3 expression and risk if GATA3 activates this enhancer, but activation direction and TOX3 expression change are not demonstrated.

predictions: Allele-specific GATA3 ChIP in MCF7 or base-edited cells shows stronger GATA3 occupancy on the T allele at this base.
GATA3 depletion reduces the alt-specific enhancer-reporter effect in breast cancer cells.
falsified_if: Controlled allele-specific assays show no GATA3 binding difference or stronger binding to the C allele.
The variant changes enhancer activity independently of the GATA3 site, or TOX3 expression is unchanged in a relevant breast-cell context.

chains.title: FOXA1 binds the alt allele more strongly at the TOX3 enhancer and modulates breast cancer risk

links.claim: FOXA1 is expressed and occupied over the variant in MCF7, and its own-model QBiC-SELEX result plus the FOXA2-mapped model detect an alt-increasing change with a strong alt site; FOXA2/FOXA3 are below 1 TPM here, so FOXA1 is the relevant forkhead factor, though ChIP is not allele-specific.

The variant lies in an active distal enhancer-like element marked by DNase and H3K27ac, compatible with FOXA1 binding at a regulatory element, although the chromatin z-scores are not MCF7-specific or allele-specific.

TOX3 is 17.5 kb away and receives high Open Targets L2G scores for breast-cancer credible sets, but the absence of a significant GTEx v8 eQTL for this variant in breast or other tissues means the enhancer-to-TOX3 link is not yet proven by expression QTL data.
MCF7 is relevant because FOXA1 is expressed there and MCF-7 FOXA1 ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant.

The T allele is the strongest reported breast-cancer effect allele and the credible set maps to TOX3, so alt-enhanced FOXA1 binding could alter TOX3 enhancer activity and risk, but FOXA1 can act context-dependently and the direction of its effect is not proven.

predictions: Allele-specific FOXA1 ChIP in MCF7 or base-edited cells shows stronger FOXA1 occupancy on the T allele at this base.
FOXA1 depletion reduces the alt-specific enhancer-reporter effect in breast cancer cells.
falsified_if: Controlled allele-specific assays show no FOXA1 binding difference or stronger binding to the C allele.
FOXA1 occupancy at the element is independent of this variant and does not affect TOX3 regulatory activity.

chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of this exact base; association is explained by linkage or another mechanism
predictions: This base has no allele-specific TF binding or enhancer-activity effect; the breast cancer signal is driven by a linked causal variant or another element.
The variant may be a passenger in a regulatory region, or the apparent regulatory signal comes from nearby sites rather than this C>T change.
falsified_if: A controlled allele-specific assay shows this exact base changes TF occupancy and enhancer activity in breast cells.
Fine-mapping and functional assays exclude linked variants and show this C>T is the causal regulatory base.

chains.title: NR2F2 binds the alt allele more strongly and may modulate TOX3 enhancer activity

links.claim: NR2F2 is expressed and occupied over the variant in MCF7, and its QBiC-SELEX collection detects a weaker alt-increasing change, but the best model is CIS-BP-mapped from PPARG and occupancy is not allele-specific, making this binding evidence weak.
The variant is in a distal enhancer-like cCRE with active chromatin marks, compatible with NR2F2 binding at a regulatory element.

TOX3 is the nearest protein-coding gene and the Open Targets L2G target for the breast-cancer credible set, but there is no breast-tissue GTEx eQTL for this variant, so the enhancer-gene link is computational.
MCF7 is relevant because NR2F2 is expressed there and MCF-7 NR2F2 ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant.
If alt-enhanced NR2F2 binding changes TOX3 enhancer activity, it could influence breast cancer risk, but NR2F2 can be context-dependent and repressive, so the phenotype direction is uncertain.

predictions: Allele-specific NR2F2 ChIP shows stronger binding to the T allele at this base in MCF7.
NR2F2 perturbation changes enhancer activity or TOX3 expression in a direction consistent with its role at this element.
falsified_if: No allele-specific NR2F2 binding is observed, or binding is not dependent on this base.
NR2F2 perturbation does not alter the enhancer or TOX3 expression in relevant breast cells.

grades_v0.reason: GATA3 ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant in MCF-7 (E06), and the QBiC-SELEX GATA3 collection detects an alt-increasing change with strong site (E20). Caveat: the strongest QBiC model is CIS-BP-mapped from GATA2, not a direct GATA3 own-model assay, and ChIP occupancy is not allele-specific.

E01 places the variant in ENSR16_9QTBS enhancer; E03 places it in dELS EH38E3180851 with DNase and H3K27ac signal. Caveat: E03 z-scores are maxima over ENCODE biosamples, not MCF7-specific or allele-specific.

E02 shows TOX3 as the nearest protein-coding gene at 17.5 kb; E16 shows Open Targets L2G assigning breast-cancer credible sets to TOX3 with high scores. This is genetic/computational target evidence, not experimental enhancer-gene proof.
E06 directly shows GATA3 is highly expressed in MCF7 (346 TPM, rank 5) and has MCF-7 ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant.

E15 supports T as the strongest breast-cancer effect allele, and E16 links the credible set to TOX3. But there is no evidence that increased GATA3 binding increases enhancer activity or TOX3 expression, so the phenotype mechanism and direction are not demonstrated.

FOXA1 ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant in MCF-7 (E05), and QBiC-SELEX reports an alt-increasing FOXA1-collection change with strong site (E21). Caveat: the best QBiC model is CIS-BP-mapped from FOXA2, so the motif evidence is indirect and not allele-specific ChIP.
E01 and E03 place the variant in an enhancer/dELS with DNase and H3K27ac signal. Caveat: the chromatin z-scores are maxima across ENCODE biosamples and are not MCF7-specific or allele-specific.

E02 places TOX3 17.5 kb away as the nearest protein-coding gene; E16 gives high Open Targets L2G scores for TOX3 in breast-cancer credible sets. This supports target assignment computationally but not a demonstrated enhancer-gene regulatory event.
E05 directly shows FOXA1 expression in MCF7 and MCF-7 ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant.

The T allele is the strongest breast-cancer effect allele in E15 and TOX3 is the L2G target in E16, but no cited evidence shows that FOXA1 binding at this base changes TOX3 expression or breast-cancer phenotype. The claim correctly hedges on FOXA1 activation direction.

NR2F2 has MCF-7 ChIP-seq occupancy over the variant (E08), but the QBiC-SELEX evidence (E22) uses a best model CIS-BP-mapped from PPARG, not an NR2F2 own-model readout, and the effect is weaker than for GATA3/FOXA1. Occupancy plus an indirect motif change is only weak support for NR2F2 allele-specific binding.
E01 and E03 place the variant in an enhancer/dELS with active chromatin marks. Caveat: active-mark z-scores are maxima over biosamples and not MCF7-specific.

E02 identifies TOX3 as the nearest protein-coding gene at 17.5 kb, and E16 assigns breast-cancer credible sets to TOX3 by L2G. This is computational/genetic support, not experimental proof of this enhancer regulating TOX3.
E08 directly shows NR2F2 expression in MCF7 and MCF-7 ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant.

E15 and E16 support a breast-cancer association and TOX3 L2G, but there is no evidence that NR2F2 binding at this base changes TOX3 expression or disease risk. The direction is especially uncertain because NR2F2 can be context-dependent and possibly repressive.

grades_final.reason: H1 binding is supported: E06 shows GATA3 ChIP-seq peaks over the variant in MCF7, and E20/E35 show alt-increased GATA3/GATA-model QBiC-SELEX binding with strong alt sites. The claim correctly notes ChIP is not allele-specific.

H1 element annotation is directly supported by E01 (ENSR16_9QTBS enhancer) and E03 (EH38E3180851 dELS with DNase/H3K27ac marks), with the caveat that the marks are biosample maxima and not allele-specific.

H1 gene link is indirect: E02 places TOX3 nearest at 17.5 kb and E16 gives high L2G TOX3 scores, but E17/E37 show no significant GTEx v8 eQTL, so enhancer-to-TOX3 regulation is not expression-QTL-proven.
H1 cell-type relevance is supported by E06: GATA3 is highly expressed in MCF7 and MCF-7 GATA3 ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant.

H1 phenotype association is strong in E15/E16, but the mechanistic direction from alt-enhanced GATA3 binding to TOX3 expression and breast-cancer risk is not demonstrated; E18a is only general review support.

H2 binding is supported: E05 shows FOXA1 ChIP-seq peaks over the variant in MCF7, and E21/E36 show alt-increased FOXA1/forkhead QBiC-SELEX binding with strong alt sites. The claim properly notes ChIP is not allele-specific.
H2 element annotation is directly supported by E01/E03/E04 for an active dELS, with the explicit caveat that the chromatin z-scores are not MCF7-specific or allele-specific.
H2 gene link is indirect: TOX3 is nearest and has high L2G support in E02/E16, but E17/E37 show no significant GTEx v8 eQTL, so enhancer-to-TOX3 regulation remains computational/genetic.
H2 cell-type relevance is supported by E05: FOXA1 is expressed in MCF7 and MCF-7 FOXA1 ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant.
H2 phenotype association is supported by E15/E16, but the claim that alt-enhanced FOXA1 binding alters TOX3 enhancer activity and breast-cancer risk is not functionally demonstrated.

H3 binding has MCF7 NR2F2 occupancy in E08 and an alt-increasing QBiC-SELEX signal in E22, but the best model is CIS-BP-mapped from PPARG, not an NR2F2 own-model change; occupancy is also not allele-specific.
H3 element annotation is directly supported by E01/E03: the variant lies in ENSR16_9QTBS and the EH38E3180851 dELS with active chromatin marks.
H3 gene link is indirect: TOX3 is nearest and L2G-supported in E02/E16, but no significant GTEx eQTL is reported in E17/E37, so the enhancer-to-TOX3 assignment is not proven.
H3 cell-type relevance is supported by E08: NR2F2 is expressed in MCF7 and MCF-7 NR2F2 ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant.
H3 phenotype link is only genetic association from E15/E16; no evidence shows that NR2F2 binding at this base changes TOX3 expression or breast-cancer risk, and the direction is explicitly uncertain.

checks.why: This would test whether GATA3 is supported by its own QBiC model or only by a GATA2-mapped model, which directly affects the strongest chain's binding link.
This would test whether FOXA1 has an own-model QBiC change or only the FOXA2-mapped prediction, which affects H2 ranking.
A breast-tissue eQTL for TOX3 would directly strengthen or weaken the variant-to-TOX3 target link shared by all three non-null chains.

Editing does not change TF occupancy or TOX3 expression, or the effect is not attributable to this base.

outcomes.outcome: No breast eQTL is present, so the TOX3 link remains L2G-based and does not distinguish GATA3 from FOXA1.
No breast eQTL is present, so the TOX3 link remains L2G-based and does not distinguish FOXA1 from GATA3.
No breast eQTL is present, so the TOX3 link remains L2G-based and does not distinguish NR2F2 from other TFs.
No breast eQTL is consistent with, but does not prove, a non-expression-mediated or linked-variant explanation.

next_experiment: Perform allele-specific GATA3 and FOXA1 ChIP-qPCR/ddPCR over the variant in MCF7 cells that are heterozygous C/T, or in isogenic MCF7 cells generated by CRISPR base editing of C>T; this is the cheapest test that directly separates the top two chains by asking which TF binds the T allele more strongly at this exact base.

QBiC-SELEX screen of chr16:52565276:C>T, one line per TF, each with the TF's own or CIS-BP-mapped model of largest |z|. Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (DepMap line ACH-000019), bound here before bound elsewhere, then a strong site before a weak one, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 10 of 95 occupied (27 with a strong site), 5 of 75 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 45 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 411 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here; 22 bound but below 1 TPM. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th. At a weak site the ChIP peak more likely reflects another site in the element.
